title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

reports.title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

summary:
Matthew and Leah Spurlock were stopped twice after their minivan’s Kansas specialty plate, number 7007, matched a stolen temporary tag on a GMC pickup. The first stop happened in Colwich, Kansas, and about a month later officers in Catoosa, Oklahoma, drew guns and handcuffed Matthew outside a casino. Kansas reuses the same plate numbers across more than 100 designs, and Flock license plate cameras only read the letters and numbers, not the background style.

Wichita police Captain Casey Slaughter said camera alerts alone are not enough for a stop, but officers must act if a stolen tag is confirmed, even when the wrong plate type was entered by another agency. Kansas is moving from six digit to seven digit plate numbers to end duplicates. The Spurlocks are no longer at risk because the stolen vehicle entry expired, but they plan to keep their 14-year-old plate.
